method_name: Unadjusted DiD with a Welch interval
checklist_markdown:
## Method name and version

Method name: Unadjusted DiD with a Welch interval

Version: v0.1.0 (commit 6f46c3cf0935776a236d3b3fa0c80ddd6bbcf95e)

## Method description

The target is the average treatment effect on the treated (ATT) in a two-period panel. For each study, subtract the control group's mean outcome change from the treated group's mean outcome change. Identification assumes no anticipation and unconditional parallel trends. The estimator does not adjust for covariates, so trends that are parallel only conditional on covariates can lead to bias.

The nominal two-sided 95% interval uses the unpooled standard error of the difference in mean changes and the Welch–Satterthwaite t critical value. Inference assumes independent units; it does not account for common cluster shocks. If both groups have zero sample variance, the reported interval has zero width.

## How to run

Use Python 3.10 or later, NumPy (>=1.24) and SciPy (>=1.10) on a CPU. No accelerator or weights are required.

```sh
git clone --branch v0.1.0 https://github.com/lisuo33/statarena-did-welch-baseline.git
cd statarena-did-welch-baseline
python -m pip install -r requirements.txt
```

With a two-period study saved as `study.npz`, run:

```sh
python did_welch.py study.npz > predictions.csv
```

For the public development split, install StatArena Lite in the same environment from your Arena checkout, replacing the example path below. Run from the baseline repository:

```sh
python -m pip install -e /path/to/Statistical-Intelligence-Arena/lite
statarena-lite run --domain did --split dev --method ./did_welch.py --output ./did-dev-predictions.csv
```

## Inputs and outputs

One row per unit. Required fields are the binary treatment indicator `D` (0 control, 1 treated) and the observed outcome change `delta_y` (post minus pre). Each field may be a vector or single-column array. The estimator requires finite values and at least two units in each group. It ignores `X`.

The Lite callable `estimate(study)` returns three numbers in order: point estimate, lower bound, upper bound. The standalone command writes `predictions.csv` with columns `table_id,estimate,ci_lower,ci_upper`, using the filename stem as the ID. The Lite command writes the same columns for all development studies to `did-dev-predictions.csv`.

## Training and data exposure

None for training, tuning or calibration. This fixed-form estimator fits no model across studies and uses no pretrained weights, outcome labels from other studies or simulation truth. Preparation used the documented StatArena Lite DiD input/output schema. Within each study, observed group indicators and outcome changes determine the estimate and interval.
